messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up: planning simultaneous py + ts publish in the next change window (tomorrow 21:00 UTC). Need eyeballs on pinning strategy and release notes. @Ben can you own the canary gating?
Maria Gomez: Docs freeze at 20:00 UTC. I'll prepare release notes + deprecation blurb for sync client removal. Need CHANGES entry and migration snippet.
Ben Patel: I can. Plan: publish TS canary -> run integration smoke -> publish Py canary. If TS major bump, we'll pin old range in examples. Also will shadow smoke on dedicated infra.
Ben Patel: publish steps I'm going to run:
```bash
# ts
npm publish --tag canary
# py (test pypi)
python -m build && twine upload dist/* --repository testpypi
```
deploy-bot: Canary publish started for @Ben (ts-client v3.0.0-alpha.1) — https://deploys.example/12345 :rocket:
deploy-bot: TS canary published, tag=canary, tarball: https://npm.example/ts-client-3.0.0-alpha.1.tgz :white_check_mark:
Ben Patel: running integration smoke against sample-repo (pin to canary).
Ben Patel: smoke failures: `TypeError: initClient(...) missing option 'timeout'` — looks like breaking change in constructor default. Investigating.
Alex Chen: that's unexpected. Did the migration guide land? @Maria
Maria Gomez: I updated README but not the migration note. I'll add constructor diff now. Also suggest we hold on Py canary until TS stabilizes.
Ben Patel: agree. I'll revert npm canary tag to previous dist-tag to avoid users hitting alpha via 'next' accidentally. Command:
```bash
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/ts-client canary
npm dist-tag add @redwood/ts-client 2.12.4 canary
```
release-bot: npm dist-tag removal and re-add requested by @Ben — queued
deploy-bot: npm tag revert completed :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: Py wheel build failed in GHA for py-client v1.7.0-alpha.1 — error log:
```
ERROR: Failed building wheel for redwood_py
...ERROR: C extension 'fastparse' failed to build
```
Canary aborted.
Ben Patel: hm, wheels failing due to new C-ext optional dep. We'll switch Py publish to sdist-only for canary to proceed, and fix wheel recipe in follow-up patch.
Alex Chen: risk assessment: sdist-only canary acceptable, but ensure we mark in release notes that wheels are pending. Maria, add note.
Maria Gomez: adding line to release notes and deprecation blurb. Also drafting a 'how to pin' section for customers: recommend `@^2.12.4` for TS and `==1.6.3` for Py until stable.
Ben Patel: Ok I will re-run Py canary with sdist tag. Command:
```bash
python -m build -s
twine upload --repository testpypi dist/*
```
deploy-bot: Py canary sdist uploaded to testpypi (1.7.0-alpha.1-sdist) :package:
Alex Chen: We need rollback plan if broad consumers hit the canary via examples. Action items:
- Ben: ensure no 'latest' tag points to canary
- Docs: update quickstarts to pin stable
- Ops: monitor @canary-usage-alert channel for spikes
I'll draft short rollback note for release channel.
Ben Patel: Done: `latest` unchanged. Also opened PR to pin examples across repos: https://github.com/redwood/example/pull/789
docs-bot: PR to docs site queued for inclusion in release notes page. Preview: https://docs-preview.example/releases/1.7.0-alpha
Alex Chen: Final sync: hold public announce until next stable cut. For now we call this a gated canary with manual hold. :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: I'll mark release as 'gated' in the changelog and push deprecation headline for sync client removal (date + migration link).
Ben Patel: Noting follow-ups: fix C-extension build, publish proper wheel, then cut stable and bump major if needed. I'll update release checklist.
Alex Chen: Thanks all. I'll update the change window calendar and post final note 1hr before 21:00 UTC. /end
